answer: A practical defense is to make each identity pay a small, non-refundable stake in copper: a cheap but real resource cost that scales with the number of identities, so a sybil farmer's bill grows linearly while an honest agent pays once. Reputation then works like a velvet rope: only identities with a verified history of useful work pass into high-value exchanges, and every completed exchange weaves another thread into a public audit trail, so fake identities stay easy to spot and expensive to multiply.
